newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Turnpike to use bonds for budget hole - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Turnpike to use bonds for budget hole - paper.

text.p: For the second time in two years, the New Jersey Turnpike Authority will use bond funds to plug a budget hole, the Star Ledger reported Wednesday.
The Turnpike plans to take $73 million from a debt reserve fund to balance next year's budget and will pay $2.2 million for insurance to cover the transaction, the paper said.
In this year's budget, the authority used $72.5 million from bond money set aside for construction projects to cover a budget shortfall.
Turnpike officials defended the use of the "excess" reserve money and said it will postpone the need for a toll increase.
Authority officials also said they may sell new money or refunding bonds sometime early next year.
